pr.title: TypingMode: merge intercrate, reveal, and defining_opaque_types
pr.description:
This adds `TypingMode` and uses it in most places. We do not yet remove `Reveal` from `param_env`s. This and other future work as tracked in #132279 and via `FIXME`s.

Fetching the `TypingMode` of the `InferCtxt` asserts that the `TypingMode` agrees with `ParamEnv::reveal` to make sure we don't introduce any subtle bugs here. This will be unnecessary once `ParamEnv::reveal` no longer exists.

As the `TypingMode` is now a part of the query input, I've merged the coherence and non-coherence caches for the new solver. I've also enabled the local `infcx` cache during coherence by clearing the cache when forking it with a different `TypingMode`.

#### `TypingMode::from_param_env`

I am using this even in cases where I know that the `param_env` will always be `Reveal::UserFacing`. This is to make it easier to correctly refactor this code in the future, any time we use `Reveal::UserFacing` in a body while not defining its opaque types is incorrect and should use a `TypingMode` which only reveals opaques defined by that body instead, cc #124598

r? @compiler-errors
pr.author: lcnr

processing.reason: The PR is an infrastructure/correctness-invariant change (introducing TypingMode and threading it through InferCtxt builders), not a MIR/data transformation with observable input→output semantics. No regression test or decoded inner MIR diff is present in the historical material. The only enforcement of the reveal/typing-mode agreement is a cfg!(debug_assertions) unreachable! panic in InferCtxt::typing_mode, and in release the mismatch silently proceeds — neither yields a deterministic defined value pair. Moreover, the frozen "incorrect transformation" is a hypothetical alternate adoption (unconditional non_body_analysis in Validator, or PostAnalysis in StateTransform), not a change in the historical PR: the PR's Validator already uses TypingMode::from_param_env(self.param_env) and StateTransform uses TypingMode::non_body_analysis(). Constructing Rust functions that return different pseudo typing-mode/reveal values would encode the conclusion by hand and manufacture a difference, which the task explicitly prohibits. No source-grounded original/transformed pair can be validated.

analysis.originalLogic: In `Validator`, the slow path builds a fresh inference context with `tcx.infer_ctxt().build()` and registers an obligation to compare trait refs after normalization. In `StateTransform::check_field_tys_sized`, the coroutine pass similarly builds `tcx.infer_ctxt().ignoring_regions().build()` and checks that coroutine field types satisfy `Sized`. Before this PR, the typing mode was implicit in the builder and did not have to agree explicitly with `ParamEnv::reveal` or carry `defining_opaque_types`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The risky adoption of the new API is to supply the wrong explicit typing mode. In `Validator`, replacing the old builder call with an unconditional `TypingMode::non_body_analysis()` rather than `TypingMode::from_param_env(self.param_env)` breaks the invariant for a `ParamEnv` whose reveal mode is `All`: the new code asserts agreement with `ParamEnv::reveal`, and outside debug builds it would continue with analysis-mode opaque handling instead of post-analysis reveal-all handling. In `StateTransform`, changing the coroutine field check from `TypingMode::non_body_analysis()` to a mode that reveals opaque types too broadly, such as `PostAnalysis` or revealing all opaque types, is not justified: the source FIXME says that if parent-defined hidden types were needed, the pass would have to reveal only the opaques defined by the parent function. The historical code is not evidence of a reproduced miscompile; this is an infrastructure/correctness-invariant change.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR after HIR type checking, especially bodies containing opaque types, RPIT/TAIT hidden types, coroutine/async field types, and trait obligations checked by MIR validation. Relevant inputs exercise both `Reveal::UserFacing` and `Reveal::All` param-envs and coroutine fields whose `Sized`-ness may depend on opaque hidden types.
analysis.summary: MIR passes that create a fresh `InferCtxt` must choose a `TypingMode` consistent with the context. `Validator` must derive it from its existing `ParamEnv` (`TypingMode::from_param_env(self.param_env)`); the coroutine `Sized` check in `StateTransform` deliberately uses `TypingMode::non_body_analysis()` and cannot assume parent-defined opaque hidden types are revealable. This is a typing-mode infrastructure change, not a demonstrated optimization or reproduced bug.
analysis.trigger: A MIR validation slow-path trait/type obligation, or a coroutine whose field types are checked for `Sized`, is evaluated with a freshly built inference context. The problem appears when the chosen `TypingMode` does not match the `ParamEnv` reveal mode or when code assumes opaque hidden types are available outside their defining body.
preconditions: The program/MIR contains opaque types or coroutine field types whose trait/Sized obligations are not resolved by fast structural checks.
A pass constructs a new `InferCtxt` rather than reusing the body's existing inference context.
The `ParamEnv` may be `Reveal::All` or may be `Reveal::UserFacing`, so the typing mode must be selected from that context.
For coroutine field checking, the coroutine may reference hidden types of opaques defined by its parent function.
pitfalls: Do not use `TypingMode::non_body_analysis()` in `Validator` when `self.param_env` is reveal-all; use `TypingMode::from_param_env(self.param_env)`.

Do not assume `non_body_analysis()` can reveal opaque types defined by the parent body; the coroutine FIXME explicitly notes that only parent-defined opaques could be revealed, and no such support exists in this change.
Do not make the coroutine check pass by globally revealing all opaques with `PostAnalysis`; that is broader than the documented future requirement.
Typing-mode mismatches are only debug assertions at `typing_mode` access time, so release builds can silently proceed with the wrong opaque-type behavior.
The patch contains no regression test changes in the supplied material; do not claim test coverage or an executed reproduction.
analysis.testStrategy: Build focused rustc UI tests around MIR validation and coroutines: (1) create a body with an opaque type and an obligation that reaches `Validator`'s slow path, compile it with reveal-all/post-analysis and with user-facing analysis param-envs, and verify the same acceptance plus no `TypingMode x Reveal mismatch` debug assertion; (2) create an async/coroutine whose field type involves an opaque hidden type defined by the parent function, and compare the coroutine `Sized` check under `non_body_analysis()` versus a deliberately broader reveal mode to pin down the documented limitation. Run a debug-enabled rustc so the `typing_mode` assertion is active, and compare diagnostics rather than claiming execution of the historical PR.
evidence: Fetching the `TypingMode` of the `InferCtxt` asserts that the `TypingMode` agrees with `ParamEnv::reveal` to make sure we don't introduce any subtle bugs here.
